<reason>A won a competitive debate by turning CON’s “no stopping rule” attack into a design dispute and then answering it with proof standards, capped/split awards, and time-limited review, while keeping the cleaner comparative: delay and record control favor the state, so closure should follow a usable remedy. B was rhetorically sharp on privacy and “grandchildren as sureties,” but kept restating an unlimited ratchet after A had fenced descendants to inherited unpaid claims, and never fully escaped A’s withheld-records fork.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first rebuttal (stronger ≠ unlimited) plus the Q1/Q2 fork on extinguishing claims while the state withholds proof; B conceded individual extensions but could not convert that into a reason to refuse one later-proved unpaid claim.</best_rebuttal>
